mechanism_narrative: WORKPLACES mobility has declined from -44.9% to -47.4% over the last four weeks, signaling sustained workplace closure or reduced occupancy. This persistent suppression of commuting activity will continue to depress retail-and-recreation visits over the next four weeks, as fewer workers means fewer incidental retail trips during commute windows.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days exceeds the mean of the last 28 days by more than 5 percentage points while WORKPLACES remains below -40%.

mechanism_narrative: PARKS mobility has stabilized around 22-46% above baseline over the last four weeks, indicating sustained outdoor recreation preference. This behavioral shift toward outdoor activities crowds out indoor retail-and-recreation visits, suppressing RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks as consumers substitute parks for enclosed shopping venues.
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS ranged from 22.3% to 46.0% over four weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC increases by more than 8 percentage points over the next 28 days while PARKS mobility remains above 20%.

mechanism_narrative: TRANSIT mobility has remained severely depressed at -55% to -62% over four weeks, indicating ongoing restrictions on public transport capacity or usage. When TRANSIT falls below -55%, retail-and-recreation venues dependent on transit-accessible footfall experience suppressed demand. This mechanism will persist over the next two weeks, keeping RETAIL_REC below baseline.
failure_condition: TRANSIT mobility recovers above -40% and RETAIL_REC fails to increase by at least 10 percentage points within two weeks.

mechanism_narrative: GROCERY_PHARM mobility has remained stable at -6% to -14% over four weeks, indicating consistent essential-goods shopping. When essential shopping is stable and RESIDENTIAL mobility remains elevated at 15-19%, consumers are sheltering in place and making only necessary trips. This regime suppresses discretionary retail-and-recreation visits over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL above 15% AND GROCERY_PHARM between -15% and 0%
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC increases by more than 12 percentage points over the next 28 days while both RESIDENTIAL remains above 15% and GROCERY_PHARM remains below -5%.

mechanism_narrative: RETAIL_REC has shown a recent recovery trend, rising from -62.1% (t-1w) to -50.3% (t-0w), a 11.8 percentage point improvement. This positive momentum in retail mobility signals emerging consumer confidence and easing behavioral caution. If this trend continues at half the rate of recent improvement, RETAIL_REC will be higher over the next four weeks than the last four weeks.
candidate_trigger: RETAIL_REC improves by more than 8 percentage points week-on-week
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is lower than the last 28 days mean of -58.0%, or declines by more than 5 percentage points in any single week.

mechanism_narrative: TRANSIT and WORKPLACES are both severely depressed (TRANSIT -55%, WORKPLACES -47%), indicating coordinated restrictions on mobility. When both transit and workplace access are constrained simultaneously, retail venues lose both commuter traffic and transit-dependent customers. Over the next two weeks, if this dual constraint persists, RETAIL_REC will remain suppressed below -45%.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC exceeds -40% over the next 14 days while both TRANSIT remains below -50% and WORKPLACES remains below -45%.

mechanism_narrative: Mid-April in London marks the onset of spring weather and Easter holiday period. PARKS mobility elevated at 22-46% reflects seasonal outdoor activity preference. Over the next four weeks (late April through mid-May), seasonal warming will further elevate PARKS mobility, sustaining the outdoor-activity substitution effect and keeping RETAIL_REC suppressed relative to the last four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS at 22.3% (t-0w), indicating spring activity surge
failure_condition: PARKS mobility falls below 10% over the next four weeks, or RETAIL_REC increases by more than 15 percentage points despite PARKS remaining above 20%.

mechanism_narrative: RETAIL_REC has recovered 11.8 percentage points from t-1w to t-0w, while TRANSIT remains severely constrained at -55%. This decoupling indicates that retail recovery is driven by local, non-transit-dependent shopping (neighborhood retail, local high streets) rather than destination retail requiring transit. Over the next week, this local-retail substitution will accelerate, lifting RETAIL_REC further as consumers shift to walkable retail.
candidate_trigger: RETAIL_REC improves week-on-week while TRANSIT remains below -50%
evidence_refs: fact:RETAIL_REC improved to -50.3% while TRANSIT at -55.0%
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC declines by more than 3 percentage points in the next week, or TRANSIT recovers above -40% without RETAIL_REC increasing by at least 5 percentage points.
